title: What is LINQ?
description: Learn what LINQ is, its purpose, and how it provides a unified query experience in C#.

data.text: **Language-Integrated Query (LINQ)** is a powerful set of technologies based on the integration of query capabilities directly into the C# language. LINQ queries are first-class language constructs in C# .NET, just like classes, methods, and events.
LINQ provides a consistent query experience to query objects (**LINQ to Objects**), relational databases (**LINQ to SQL**), and XML (**LINQ to XML**).

LINQ is a uniform query syntax in C# and VB.NET to retrieve data from different sources and formats. It is integrated directly into C#, thereby eliminating the mismatch between programming languages and databases, as well as providing a single querying interface for different types of data sources.

For example, SQL is a Structured Query Language used to save and retrieve data from a database. In the same way, LINQ is a structured query syntax built into C# and VB.NET to retrieve data from different types of data sources such as collections, ADO.NET DataSet, XML documents, web services, and MS SQL Server.

data.text: LINQ queries return results as **objects**. This enables you to use an object-oriented approach on the result set without worrying about transforming different formats of results into objects.
The following example demonstrates a simple LINQ query that retrieves all strings from an array that contain the letter 'a'.

data.text: In the example above, the string array `names` is the data source. The LINQ query is assigned to a variable `myLinqQuery`. You do not get the result of a LINQ query until you execute it.

LINQ queries can be executed in multiple ways. In this example, we use a `foreach` loop to execute the query stored in `myLinqQuery`. The `foreach` loop executes the query on the data source and retrieves the result, then iterates over the result set.

data.title: Important
data.text: Every LINQ query must query some kind of data source, whether it is an array, collection, XML, or database. After writing a LINQ query, it must be executed to get the result.
The example query uses the **query syntax** of LINQ. Every LINQ query consists of three main parts:

items: **Data source** — The collection, array, or database to query from
**Query** — The filtering, sorting, and projection operations
**Execution** — The mechanism to actually run the query and get results

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: LINQ integrates query capabilities directly into C#
LINQ provides a unified syntax for querying objects, databases, and XML
LINQ queries return results as objects
Queries must be executed (e.g., via foreach) to get results
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to understand why LINQ was created and its advantages over traditional approaches.
